Inside: tables and text boxes, contact info in headers, skills as icons, creative section titles, missing JD keywords, unexpanded acronyms and risky file types, each with a fix, plus a recap.

slides.headline: YOUR RESUME NEVER REACHED HUMANS
slides.body: 7 habits that can sink it in the ATS scan.

slides.headline: SOFTWARE READS IT FIRST
slides.body: Many ATS parse your file into fields, then rank it. A scrambled parse can rank low before a recruiter looks.

slides.headline: DROP TABLES AND TEXT BOXES
slides.body: Some parsers read across columns and mix your lines together.

slides.headline: KEEP CONTACT INFO IN THE BODY
slides.body: Many ATS skip page headers and footers. Put your name, email and phone in the main text.

slides.headline: WRITE SKILLS AS WORDS
slides.body: A logo or star rating can't be read as text. Type the skill name.

slides.headline: MATCH THE JOB DESCRIPTION
slides.body: Many ATS rank by keyword match. Use the JD's exact terms where they're true for you.

slides.headline: SPELL OUT ACRONYMS ONCE
slides.body: The JD might search for either form. Give it both.

slides.headline: SEND A FILE IT CAN READ
slides.body: Follow the posting. If it doesn't say, a .docx or text-based PDF is safest.

slides.headline: SAVE THIS
slides.body: Run the checklist on your resume before the next application.

caption:
One 2-column table can sink your resume before a recruiter opens it.

Many companies run applications through an applicant tracking system first. It pulls your file apart into fields like name, job titles and skills, then ranks you against the job description. If the parse goes wrong, a strong candidate can look like a weak match.

The usual culprits are small. A two-column table. Your email sitting in the page header. Skills shown as logos. A section called My Story instead of Work Experience. These ATS resume problems are easy to miss because the page looks fine to you.

Keywords matter too. If the job post says Salesforce and stakeholder management, and your resume says CRM tools and working with teams, a keyword ranker may not connect them. Use their words where they're true for you.

Workday, Greenhouse, Lever and Taleo don't all parse the same way, so treat these as resume tips that lower the risk, not guarantees. The quickest check: paste your resume into a plain text file and see what survives.

Save this for your next application.
